text:
anna: heads up — the JS quickstart sample uses `const Redwood = require('redwood-inference')` and `module.exports = ...` which flat-out fails in edge runtimes that expect ESM. Anyone else hit this?

alex: saw that earlier. edge (Vercel Edge / Cloudflare Workers) needs `import` and we also have ambiguity in how we export (default vs named). Users get a `.default` wrapper sometimes.

maria: yeah this comes from shipping both CJS and an ESM build without clear docs. For ESM consumers you can end up with `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` vs `import * as Redwood` confusion. Docs don't call this out, sorry.

sam: @maria can we add a note in the JS quickstart + sample app about recommended import styles, and show both `require` (Node) and `import` (ESM/edge) examples? Quick snippet for edge would help.

maria: good idea. We actually have an `edge` entrypoint (e.g. `redwood-inference/edge`) but it's not linked from quickstart. I'll surface that and add examples.

tyler: also ran into auth friction in the sample: the edge demo uses `REDWOOD_API_KEY` but it's not picked up in Cloudflare / Vercel the same way as `process.env`. That tripped me up.

alex: right — edge runtimes often don't expose `process.env`. Vercel uses env vars you inject at build/runtime, Cloudflare uses secrets bound to the worker. Need provider-specific snippet and a suggestion to pass the key at client init as fallback.

maria: also an important DX bug: streaming + retry logic is weird on edge. If you stream and the connection fails, automatic retries aren't possible. We should document that streaming responses are non-retriable and recommend checkpointing or returning short responses.

anna: minimal repro I used in the sample app — maybe useful for docs: \n```js\n// edge example (doesn't use process.env)\nimport Redwood from 'redwood-inference/edge'\nconst client = new Redwood({ apiKey: globalThis.REDWOOD_API_KEY || 'override-at-init' })\nawait client.generate('hello from edge')\n```\n
sam: nice. Maybe sample repo can detect `globalThis.Deno` / `globalThis.fetch` and show which pattern to use. Also mention `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'` for tree-shaking.

maria: action items: 1) update quickstart with ESM/CJS section + examples for `require` vs `import` and default vs named; 2) add an "edge" quickstart with provider snippets (Vercel, Cloudflare, Netlify); 3) clarify auth patterns and example for passing key at client init; 4) add a short note about streaming/retries; 5) improve TS types for edge entrypoint (no more `any`). I'll open a docs PR and link it here.

tyler: can we also add a tiny checklist in the sample app README for new devs (env binding steps per provider)? onboarding friction would drop a lot.

maria: agreed — docs PR will include a quick checklist and a change in the demo repo to show both node and edge entrypoints.

docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 :sparkles: (includes ESM/CJS notes, edge snippets, auth guidance, and TS typing fixes)

anna: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. I'll patch the sample app and flag the demo with a note about streaming limitations until we have a robust retry story.

alex: small follow-up — can we add a short troubleshooting section: "If you see `.default` on import, try `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` or `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference/esm'` depending on runtime." That saved me earlier.

maria: will add that exact troubleshooting text to the FAQ in the PR.

sam: great. documenting these edge cases is going to cut down onboarding tickets a ton.

anna: agreed. end of thread.
